question: Can one Windows ARM64 host produce a correct, signed x64 package, so that a single self-hosted runner can cover both shipped architectures?

build.updaterSigningKey: throwaway key generated outside the repository; never committed

peMachineTypeMeaning: IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64, so the packaged executable is genuinely x64 and not an ARM64 binary with x64 naming

alsoVerified.note: A Rust test binary built for x86_64-pc-windows-msvc runs on this host under Windows x64 emulation and reports std::env::consts::ARCH as x86_64. Emulation is one-directional: an x64 host cannot execute ARM64 binaries.

limits: This proves the x64 package builds, signs, and reports the correct machine type when cross-built from an ARM64 host. It is not installation, capture, OCR, overlay, or runtime evidence on x64 hardware, and it does not replace the manual Windows gate.
